result.summary: I added JMAK command support over TCP and SMS. The new class org.traccar.protocol.JmakProtocolEncoder has the constructor (Protocol protocol, boolean textChannel). Over TCP it writes `$<id>;<value>;|...#`. Over SMS it writes `JMAK#<action>;<id>;<value>#...`, and reboot is the literal text `JMAK#REBOOT#`. The class extends StringProtocolEncoder because BaseProtocol.setTextCommandEncoder only accepts that type. JmakProtocol now registers the encoder in the TCP pipeline (with a StringEncoder) and as the SMS text encoder. It lists the same 12 commands for data and for text. Set connection uses parameter 13 when the server is an IPv4 address and parameter 43 otherwise, then parameter 12 for the port. The task did not name a command type for the movement alarm, so I mapped it to the existing Command.TYPE_ALARM_VIBRATION with KEY_DATA, the same way MiniFinder uses it. Speed limit and odometer take their value from KEY_DATA, as other encoders do. All specification examples are in the new tests and pass. The full test suite and checkstyle (main and test) also pass when run with JDK 25.

changes.summary: New encoder for the TCP format and the SMS format. Covers custom, engine stop/resume, output control (index 1/2/3 to params 34/94/167), periodic positions, odometer, set connection (IP or domain, then port), reboot, speed limit, battery, power removal and movement alarms.
Registers the supported data and text commands, sets the SMS text encoder (textChannel=true), and adds StringEncoder and the TCP encoder (textChannel=false) to the pipeline.
New tests for every command over TCP and over SMS, including all specification examples, plus one test that writes through the channel.

acceptance.criterion: The commands are encoded as described, over TCP and over SMS
acceptance.evidence: JmakProtocolEncoderTest asserts every command in both modes, including `$34;1;#`, `$43;jmak.com.br;|12;5259;#`, `JMAK#s;13;191.233.246.121#s;12;5259#`, `JMAK#e;57;0#` and `JMAK#REBOOT#`. All 3 tests pass.

acceptance.criterion: The change is covered by tests
acceptance.evidence: New file src/test/java/org/traccar/protocol/JmakProtocolEncoderTest.java with 3 tests (TCP, TCP through the channel, SMS).

acceptance.criterion: The existing test suite still passes
acceptance.evidence: `./gradlew test checkstyleMain checkstyleTest --offline` with JAVA_HOME=openjdk@25 exited 0. None of the 429 test result files contains a failure or an error.

human_needed.question: Which command type should the JMAK 'movement alarm' use? I used the existing alarmVibration (TYPE_ALARM_VIBRATION) with the value from 'data'.
human_needed.why: The specification names no Traccar command type for it. A dedicated type such as 'movementAlarm' would need a new constant and a change in the web UI.

harness_used: Existing encoders and tests used as patterns: WondexProtocol/WondexProtocolEncoder/WondexProtocolEncoderTest (data plus text encoder), MiniFinderProtocolEncoder (TYPE_ALARM_VIBRATION with KEY_DATA), GatorProtocolEncoder (KEY_DATA for speed limit and odometer)
Gradle test and checkstyle tasks (checkstyle caught an import-order problem)

harness_gaps.problem: The build needs Java 21 or newer, but the default JDK on this machine is 17 and the repo does not document this. I had to set JAVA_HOME to /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@25 by hand.

There is no agent or contributor doc (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING) that explains how to add a protocol encoder. Two rules had to be found by reading code: setTextCommandEncoder needs a StringProtocolEncoder, and the SMS path calls encodeCommand(Command) without a channel.
In the task text, the TCP command prefix (`$`) was replaced by a copy of the prompt. I inferred it from the example `$34;1;#`.
The submodule is empty, so I could not check how the UI labels the command types (for example alarmVibration and alarmRemove).
